task_instance: Refactor an over-specialized, entity-named UI: two parallel smart select components (EpicSelect, MilestoneSelect) that each fetch their own data and differ only by copy/icon/entity type/query hook/test-id. Apply the skill's core rules to collapse them into one configurable primitive named by responsibility (GroupingSelect in src/core/ui), push data sourcing out to the caller, and leave thin feature adapters, then verify behavior is preserved.
evidence: Built a self-contained TypeScript sample in the work directory. BEFORE: before/src/features/epics/EpicSelect.ts and before/src/features/milestones/MilestoneSelect.ts, each embedding its own query hook and differing only by entity type/label/icon/test-id (the skill's 'two files, same story', 'query-in-component', and 'entity-name' smells). Applied the skill's core deliverable to produce AFTER: after/src/core/ui/GroupingSelect.ts (Rule 1 named by responsibility, Rule 4 promoted to src/core/ui, Rule 3 receives data instead of fetching, Rule 6 config-driven not branch-driven); thin adapters after/src/features/epics/epicGrouping.ts and after/src/features/milestones/milestoneGrouping.ts that map value shape + copy/icon only and preserve the stable test-id contract; and after/src/features/planning/PlanningToolbar.ts as the caller that owns data fetching (useEpicsQuery/useMilestonesQuery) and feeds the single GroupingSelect. Verified two ways: (1) typecheck -- ran the preinstalled tsc (tsc -p tsconfig.json, strict mode) which printed TYPECHECK_OK with no errors; (2) behavior-preservation test after/test/verify.ts run with bun, which asserted the refactored epic and milestone outputs render identically to the old EpicSelect/MilestoneSelect, that the two cases differ only by config, and that both are produced by the same GroupingSelect primitive -- all four checks printed PASS and 'ALL CHECKS PASSED'. The refactor collapses the duplicate entity-named variants into one generic primitive with data sourcing lifted to the caller, which is the skill's stated output standard. Note: the skill's optional step-9 project tools (ui-testability-contract scan, FTA cap check, project eslint config) are repo-specific and not part of this skill's files; they were not needed to produce or verify the core deliverable.
